recentItems.title: Robot Rentals Heating up in China
recentItems.description:
In central China's Hubei Province robot rentals are surging this summer; their popularity rising thanks to appearances at shopping malls and their proliferation at cultural and tourism sites.

Engineers at a robot rental company set up a pair of humanoids at a mall in the region's capital Wuhan recently, where a small crowd of onlookers gathered to interact with them.

China's robot market is more than just humanoids.

It also includes things like exoskeleton suits that assist travelers when climbing the steep hills or mountains often found at tourism destinations.

Experts say that the robot rental market in China is expected to reach 1.5 billion U.S. dollars this year.

recentItems.title: China Accelerates Its Push for Fusion Energy As Next-Gen Artificial Sun Project Takes Shape
recentItems.description:
China's plans to develop a fusion power source that would provide clean non-stop energy like the sun, is taking shape.

Work has been ongoing across several regions.

In eastern China's Hefei City, the Burning Plasma Experimental Superconducting Tokamak, or BEST, has moved into a final stage of construction with completion set for next year.

Over a thousand kilometers away in southwest China's Chengdu, a fusion innovation hub is in the works.

Spanning 320 hectares, it will house national R&D centers, major facilities and private firms.

The plan is to build five innovation platforms to service more than 50 industry-chain enterprises, and drive the fusion power industry scale beyond 3 billion U.S. dollars in the next three to five years.

Under the current research plan, BEST aims to achieve a fusion power output of 20 to 200 megawatts, with the goal of demonstrating fusion based electricity generation by the year 2030.
